questions.q: Which pin marks the pharyngeal tonsil, called the adenoid when enlarged?
questions.explain: Pharyngeal tonsil: aggregated lymphoid tissue in the roof and posterior wall of the nasopharynx. Enlarged, it is the adenoid. Palatine tonsils sit in the oropharynx.

questions.q: Which pin marks the torus tubarius, the raised rim of the auditory tube opening?
questions.explain: Torus tubarius: the raised area of the pharyngotympanic tube. The pharyngeal recess is the area just behind it.

questions.q: Which pin marks the only pharyngeal muscle supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve?
questions.explain: Stylopharyngeus (CN IX) is the exception. The constrictors and cricopharyngeus are vagus. Tensor veli palatini (a palate muscle) is V3.

questions.q: Which pin marks the cricoid cartilage?
questions.explain: Cricoid: a complete ring at C6, felt below the laryngeal prominence. The lecture calls it the most limiting airway structure for intubation.

questions.q: Which pin marks the true vocal fold?
questions.explain: Vocal folds: elastic true cords attached to the arytenoid cartilages. Vestibular folds are inelastic and lie superior to them.

questions.q: Which pin marks the vallecula, where the intubation blade goes?
questions.explain: Vallecula: the space between the epiglottis and the root of the tongue.

questions.q: Which pin marks a parathyroid gland?
questions.explain: Four parathyroids lie on the posterior surface of the thyroid lobes. The inferior thyroid arteries mainly supply them.

questions.q: Which pin marks the carina?
questions.explain: Carina: the internal ridge at the tracheal bifurcation, at T5 or the sternal angle (2nd rib).

questions.q: Which pin marks the inferior thyroid artery?
questions.explain: Inferior thyroid artery: arises from the thyrocervical trunk (off the subclavian). It also feeds the parathyroids and the cervical esophagus. The superior thyroid artery comes from the external carotid.

questions.q: A patient has lost the afferent limb of the gag reflex. Which nerve carries sensation from the pharyngeal mucosa?
questions.explain: CN IX gives sensory fibers to the mucous membrane of the pharynx (gag reflex, food bolus). CN X is the motor nerve of the pharynx.

questions.q: Sensation from the anterior and superior nasopharynx is carried mainly by which nerve?
questions.explain: Anterior and superficial viscerocranial structures use CN V; deeper pharyngeal structures use CN IX. The anterior, superior nasopharynx is V2.

questions.q: A muscle tenses the palate and pulls on the auditory tube when swallowing. Which nerve supplies it?
questions.explain: Tensor veli palatini is supplied by V3. It tenses the palate, seals the oral cavity from the nasal cavity, and helps equalize middle-ear pressure.

questions.q: Pharyngeal venous plexus blood drains through the pharyngeal and superior thyroid veins into which vein?
questions.explain: External palatine vein, then pharyngeal venous plexus, then pharyngeal and superior thyroid veins, then the internal jugular vein.

questions.q: The ascending pharyngeal artery and the superior thyroid artery both arise from which artery?
questions.explain: Both are branches of the external carotid artery.

questions.q: According to the lecture, which laryngeal structure is most limiting for intubation because it does not move and is small?
questions.explain: The cricoid, the complete ring at C6, is the most limiting structure of the airway for intubation per the lecture.

questions.q: Which muscle abducts (opens) the vocal folds?
questions.explain: Posterior cricoarytenoid: the openers (abduction). Lateral cricoarytenoid: the closers (adduction). Cricothyroid and vocalis are not the cord openers.

questions.q: Which landmark separates the upper from the lower respiratory tract, so tracheitis counts as a lower respiratory infection?
questions.explain: The lecture note: the vocal cords separate upper from lower respiratory tract. Tracheitis lies below them, so it is a lower respiratory infection.

questions.q: A 62-year-old has hoarseness as the only symptom of a thoracic aortic arch aneurysm. Which nerve is stretched?
questions.explain: The left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks under the aortic arch. The right one hooks under the right subclavian artery.

questions.q: After thyroid surgery a patient has a raspy voice. Which nerve passes beside the ligament of Berry?
questions.explain: The recurrent laryngeal nerve usually passes between the ligament of Berry and its lateral leaf, or deep to the ligament.

questions.q: Each tracheal cartilage is C-shaped. Which structure connects the open posterior ends?
questions.explain: The trachealis muscle bridges the posterior gap and allows constriction and dilation. Annular ligaments join one ring to the next.

questions.q: Which arteries supply the cervical esophagus?
options: Esophageal branches of the inferior thyroid arteries
Branches of the superior thyroid arteries
Branches of the internal carotid arteries
questions.explain: Esophageal branches of the inferior thyroid arteries (ascending and descending). Veins drain to the inferior thyroid veins, then brachiocephalic veins, then the SVC.

questions.q: Which thyroid cells produce calcitonin?
questions.explain: Thyroid C (parafollicular) cells make calcitonin. Follicular cells (thyrocytes) make thyroxine (T4), and the follicles store colloid, the thyroglobulin used to make T4.

questions.q: The cricopharyngeal part of the inferior constrictor serves as which structure, and which nerve supplies it?
questions.explain: The cricopharyngeal part of the inferior constrictor acts as the superior esophageal sphincter (not a true sphincter, per her note). Like all the constrictors it is vagus.

questions.q: Vasomotor fibers to the cervical esophagus travel in which structure?
questions.explain: Cervical esophagus: motor fibers come via branches of the recurrent laryngeal nerves (CN X), and vasomotor fibers via the cervical sympathetic trunks.

questions.q: Which thyroid veins drain into the left and right brachiocephalic veins?
questions.explain: Superior and middle thyroid veins drain to the internal jugular vein. Inferior thyroid veins drain to the left and right brachiocephalic veins.

questions.q: How is parathyroid hormone secretion mainly controlled?
questions.explain: Parathyroid secretion is controlled hormonally, not by nerves. Nerve branches from the sympathetic ganglia and vagus are only vasomotor.
